model.about: A model is a JSON file (.ographis) with nodes and the connections between their ports. Each node has a type from node_types, an id that is unique in the model, a name that is shown, x and y on the canvas, and params by the keys of its type. A connection goes from [node id, output port] to [node id, input port]. An input port may take several connections: their streams are put together, except on ports that keep them apart, such as Layers of Draw map. Settings that are not given take their default. $(name) in a setting is the value of the variable name. Check a model with og check.

expressions.about: As the field calculator of QGIS: attributes by name or in "double quotes", text in 'single quotes'. Operators: + - * / // % || = <> < <= > >= AND OR NOT IS NULL IN LIKE ILIKE, CASE WHEN … THEN … ELSE … END. $area, $length and $perimeter in m² and m, $x, $y and $id.

node_types.title: Read files named in an attribute
node_types.description: Reads the file whose path is in an attribute of each feature, such as the answers HTTP request keeps as files: GeoJSON, GeoTIFF and anything Input reads. The features of each file get the attributes of its row; grids are put together into one.

params.label: Path in
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute with the path of each file, such as _file from HTTP request

params.label: Cells as
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: An image: shown as a picture, a click gives the values of a cell
Heights or other values on a grid, for terrain

params.hint: For rasters, such as GeoTIFF. Grids of several files are put together into one

params.label: Coordinate system
params.hint: For files that do not say. Empty: as the files say

node_types.title: Input
node_types.description: Reads a file, a folder of files or a web address: geodata, tables, rasters, CAD drawings, city and building models, 3D models and point clouds. The formats are listed when nothing is selected. With a stream connected to Paths, it reads the file each feature names instead, such as the answers HTTP request keeps as files; the features of each file get the attributes of its row, and grids are put together into one.

params.label: File or folder
params.shape: a file, a folder, a pattern with * or a web address; relative paths start at the folder of the model
params.hint: A file, also zipped; a folder, whose files that match the filter are read as one; or a web address (https://…)

params.label: Paths from
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: With a stream connected to Paths: the attribute with the path of each file to read, such as _file from HTTP request. The file or folder above is then not used

params.label: The address is
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF: read where it is
COPC point cloud: read where it is

params.hint: A service is read through its own pages, and only what reaches into a rectangle when one is set: OGC API Features (/collections), WFS, or an ArcGIS FeatureServer. A GeoTIFF (.tif) and a COPC point cloud (.copc.laz) are read where they are: only the rectangle, and a GeoTIFF from its overviews when read coarser

params.label: API connection
params.shape: the name of an API connection in the settings of the user
params.hint: A key or a login for the address, kept in the settings. Where the key goes in the address, write {{key}}

params.label: Keep the fetched file
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: No fetches the file again in every run. Yes fetches it once and reads the copy after that

params.label: Files in the folder
params.hint: A filter such as *.shp. Several are separated by semicolons

params.label: Include subfolders
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: File in the zip
params.hint: Such as roads.gpkg, data/roads.gpkg or *.gpkg. Empty: the Shapefiles in it, or else the first data file

params.label: Layers
params.shape: names of layers of the file in path, separated by commas; empty reads the first, * all
params.hint: Tables in a GeoPackage, sheets in Excel. Empty reads the first one, * reads all

params.label: First row has names (Excel)
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Read
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Only what reaches into a rectangle is read. In a GeoPackage, through its spatial index, which is quick

params.label: West, smallest x
params.hint: A number such as 290000, or a variable of the model such as $(xmin)

params.label: South, smallest y
params.hint: Such as 6390000 or $(ymin)

params.label: East, largest x
params.hint: Such as 340000 or $(xmax)

params.label: North, largest y
params.hint: Such as 6420000 or $(ymax)

params.label: Rectangle in
params.hint: The coordinate system of the rectangle. Empty: that of the data

params.label: Largest number of features
params.hint: Reads only the first ones, for example 1000, to try a model out on large data. Empty reads all

params.label: Cells as
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: An image: shown as a picture, a click gives the values of a cell
Heights or other values on a grid, for terrain

params.hint: Points and squares get the values of the bands. The outline is one area with the size of the raster. An image is shown as a picture on the map under the canvas, and a click on it tells the values of the cell in every band; a large raster is read smaller. A grid keeps the values of the first band for Shade terrain and Quick terrain view

params.label: Level of detail
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The coarsest: the first tiles from the top
The finest: the tiles at the bottom

params.hint: Which tiles of the tree are read. The finest of a large tileset can be very many: read within a rectangle, or down to an error

params.label: Largest error, in metres
params.hint: Tiles are read down to where the tileset says they are this close to the finest. A smaller number is more detail and more tiles

params.label: At most this many tiles
params.hint: More is an error that says so, rather than a long wait

params.label: Zoom level of the vector tiles
params.hint: Such as 14. A higher level has more detail and more tiles. Empty: the most detailed in a file, 14 on the web

params.label: Features the tiles cut apart
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Kept as pieces, one per tile

params.hint: Tiles cut a lake or a road at their edges. Put together, each is one feature again: the pieces with the same mvt_id and values

params.label: Coordinate system to place them in
params.hint: Such as EPSG:3006 for SWEREF 99 TM. Empty is the UTM zone where the tiles are

params.label: Move the heights by
params.hint: 3D Tiles have their heights above the ellipsoid. In Sweden the geoid lies some 20 to 40 metres above it, so for heights in RH 2000 write the geoid height of the place with a minus, such as −32

params.label: Only these classes
params.hint: Such as 2 for the ground, or 2, 6, 9 for ground, buildings and water. Empty reads all: 1 unclassified, 3 to 5 vegetation, 7 and 18 noise, 17 bridges

params.label: Every n-th point
params.hint: Thins a dense cloud: 10 reads one point in ten. 1 reads all

params.label: Spacing between points (COPC)
params.hint: For a COPC file: only the levels of its octree down to about this many metres between points, such as 2 for an overview. Empty reads all. With a rectangle, only that part is read, also from the web

params.label: Units of the model
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: As the format says, or from its size

params.hint: glTF is in metres, and 3MF and STEP say theirs. OBJ files do not say: more than 200 across is taken as centimetres. STL is taken as millimetres

params.label: Upwards in the model
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: As the format says: y for glTF, z for OBJ, STL, 3MF and STEP

params.hint: A building lying on its side has the other

params.label: Blocks
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: A block, such as a well or a tree, as a point with its name and the values of its attributes as columns, or drawn out in lines

params.label: Closed polylines
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Such as the outlines of buildings

params.label: Level of detail

params.hint: Of each city object in CityGML and CityJSON: LoD1 is blocks, LoD2 has roof shapes, LoD3 windows and more

params.label: Openings
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Spaces

params.hint: The rooms as volumes. They fill the building, so they are left out unless asked for

params.label: Property sets

params.label: Upwards in the scene
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: As the format says: y down for PLY, y up for SPZ
y down, as COLMAP and the training of splats
y up, as three.js and many viewers

params.label: Origin of the model, east
params.hint: Where 0, 0, 0 of the model goes on the map, such as 319500 in SWEREF 99 TM

params.label: Origin of the model, north
params.hint: Such as 6399800

params.label: Origin of the model, height
params.hint: The height of the ground, such as 52.5

params.label: Turned clockwise, in degrees
params.hint: Seen from above, around the origin

params.label: Tags as attributes
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The common ones; the rest stay in other_tags

params.hint: Each tag of OpenStreetMap, such as amenity or opening_hours, can become an attribute of its own. A whole country has thousands of different tags, so by default only those on at least one feature in a hundred get a column, and the rest stay together in other_tags, as GDAL reads them

params.label: Records at (JSON, XML)
params.hint: Where the list of records is in the file, such as results or data.items, or in XML the elements by their path, such as Fastigheter.Fastighet. Empty finds it: the list itself, or a list such as results

params.label: Objects in a record (JSON, XML)
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Attributes of their own, lists as JSON text
Attributes of their own, lists too

params.label: Cell size

params.label: Coordinate system
params.hint: Used when the file does not state its own

params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Windows-1252: Western Europe, as Swedish files from Windows

params.label: X column (CSV)
params.hint: Empty looks for x, lon, e, east

params.label: Y column (CSV)
params.hint: Empty looks for y, lat, n, north

params.label: WKT column (CSV)
params.hint: Empty looks for wkt, geom, geometry

params.label: Delimiter (CSV)
params.hint: Empty detects ; , tab or |

params.hint: Each feature gets an attribute that says which file it came from. The name of the attribute can be changed

params.label: File name as
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Add the layer name as an attribute
params.shape: the name of an attribute to add, or empty for none
params.hint: Each feature gets an attribute with the name of the layer or sheet it came from. The name of the attribute can be changed

node_types.title: View
node_types.description: A place to look at data: connect as many streams as you like to it, from anywhere in the model. Click it, and each connection is shown under the canvas, in the table and on the map, by its number and name. It writes nothing.

node_types.title: Make zip file
node_types.description: Packs what the outputs of the model wrote in the run into one zip file, all or those named, with other files and folders you choose, such as a description or terms of use. It runs when everything else in the model has run, and needs no connection.

params.label: Zip file
params.shape: a file to write; relative paths start at the folder of the model
params.hint: Such as out/result.zip. {now('%Y-%m-%d')} puts the date in the name

params.label: From the outputs
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: What the outputs named below wrote

params.hint: The files they wrote in this run, all of a Shapefile together

params.label: Outputs by name
params.hint: The names of the outputs, separated by ;

params.label: Other files and folders
params.shape: files and folders: a list of strings, or one string separated by ;; relative paths start at the folder of the model
params.hint: Such as README.txt, docs/terms.pdf or the folder styles, which goes in with all it holds. A new row comes when one is filled in

params.label: In the zip file
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: In their folders, as under the folder of the model
All in the top of the zip file

node_types.title: Output
node_types.description: Writes the stream to GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON, Excel, LibreOffice Calc, CSV or txt. A file that already exists is overwritten, but in a GeoPackage or a workbook only the layer or sheet that is written. A Shapefile holds one geometry type, so mixed streams are split into several files. A workbook can be given a font, a bold and locked top row and colours. A map from Draw map is written as PNG, JPG, GeoTIFF or a PDF page.

params.label: File
params.shape: a file to write; relative paths start at the folder of the model
params.hint: An attribute or an expression in braces gives a file for each value: out/{municipality}.gpkg, or stops_{now('%Y-%m-%d')}.xlsx

params.label: Format
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Google Sheets (the address of the sheet)
Web map with Leaflet or MapLibre (a folder)

params.hint: The file gets the extension of the format

params.label: Layer
params.hint: Table in a GeoPackage, sheet in a workbook. Empty uses the file name. Other layers and sheets in the file are kept. {municipality} gives one for each value

params.label: Encoding
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: For Shapefile and CSV

params.label: Decimal comma (CSV)
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Geometry (CSV, Excel)
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: x and y for points, WKT for the rest

params.label: If it is already there
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: The table in a GeoPackage, the sheet in a workbook, or the file. New features are matched to the attributes that are there by name

params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Group by
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: glTF: the objects of each value under a parent of its own, such as the kind of building, to show and hide together in Blender

params.label: Materials by
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: glTF: a material named after each value, such as the material of the roof, to give them all a new look at once in Blender

params.hint: Text to put between the values, such as a space or _ . Empty puts nothing

params.label: Skip empty values
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: An empty value then gives no separator either

params.label: Fixed texts are
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Parts, with the separator around them too
Separators of their own, each between two values

params.hint: As separators of their own, different ones can go between different attributes, such as code, ' - ', name, ', ', town

node_types.title: Change case
node_types.description: Makes the text of the chosen attributes UPPER CASE, lower case, with the first letter capital, or every word capital: SKÖVDE, skövde, Skövde, Lilla Edet.

params.label: In attributes
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas

params.label: Make it
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Every word capital also counts the parts of names with - as words, as in Dals-Ed

node_types.title: Replace text
node_types.description: Replaces a text with another in the chosen attributes: every A becomes B, or every space becomes nothing.

params.label: In attributes
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas

params.label: Find
params.hint: The text to replace. Spaces count

params.label: Replace with
params.hint: Empty removes what was found

params.label: Tell A from a
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Split attribute
node_types.description: Splits a text at a character, such as a comma or $. The parts become attributes of their own, or one feature each.

params.label: Attribute
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port

params.label: Split at
params.hint: A character or a text, for example , ; $ or |. Write \t for a tab

params.label: Parts go
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Into attributes suits a fixed pattern, such as Göteborg$1480. One feature per part suits a list, such as 1,4,7, that is then filtered, joined or counted

params.label: New name
params.hint: Into attributes: the start of the new names. One feature per part: the attribute the part goes in. Empty uses the name of the split attribute

params.label: Largest number of parts
params.hint: The last part keeps the rest. Empty splits at every one

params.label: Remove spaces around the parts
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Keep empty parts
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: As in a,,b

params.label: Number attribute
params.hint: One feature per part: an attribute with the number of the part, 1, 2 and so on. Empty adds none

node_types.title: Manage attributes
node_types.description: Keeps, removes, renames and orders attributes, and creates new ones.

params.label: Attributes
params.shape: a list of {"name": attribute, "action": "keep" | "rename" | "remove", "to": new name}
params.hint: Keep, rename or remove each one. The arrows change the order

params.label: Attributes that are not listed
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Those that come in later, when what comes before this step is changed

params.label: New attributes
params.hint: A value is an expression: 'text' in single quotes, a number, or for example population / 1000

node_types.title: Join by attribute
node_types.description: Joins attributes from Supplier where the key matches, as a join in SQL: inner, only those that match; left, all of Requestor; or full, all of both. The first match, or every match as one to many. The geometry comes from Requestor, and its attributes win when names clash, unless Supplier's are given a prefix. The number 1480 and the text 1480 count as the same key.

params.label: Requestor key
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: One or more attributes

params.label: Supplier key
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: As many as in Requestor

params.label: Join
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Inner: only those that match, in Merged
Left: all of Requestor, those without a match with empty attributes
Full: all of both, Supplier without a match too

params.hint: As in SQL. Those left out still come out on their own ports

params.label: When several match
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The first match: one feature for each in Requestor
Every match: a feature for each pair, one to many

params.label: Prefix for Supplier's attributes
params.hint: Such as s_. With a prefix, attributes of Supplier with the same name as one of Requestor are taken too, under the new name

node_types.title: Sort
node_types.description: Sorts the features by one or more attributes. Numbers sort as numbers, text without regard to case. Empty values come last.

params.label: Sort by
params.hint: The first attribute decides, the next breaks ties, and so on. Each has its own order. Empty values always come last

node_types.title: Calculate statistics
node_types.description: Counts features and calculates sum, min, max, mean, median and percentiles of numeric attributes, for the whole stream or per group. Summary has one row per group, Complete has every feature with the figures of its group.

params.label: Attributes to analyse
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Numbers. Empty only counts features

params.label: Group by
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Empty gives one summary for the whole stream

params.label: Percentiles
params.hint: Such as 10, 90 for the values a tenth lie below and a tenth above, as _p10 and _p90. Empty gives none

node_types.title: Keep attributes
node_types.description: Keeps the attributes you choose and removes all others. Quicker than Manage attributes when only a few of many are wanted.

params.label: Attributes to keep
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: All others are removed. The order stays as it was

node_types.title: Intersect
node_types.description: Cuts points, lines and areas by the areas of Overlay. Each part that lies in an area gets the attributes of both and goes to Intersection: a road cut where it crosses from one zone to the next. Where the areas overlap, a part comes for each. What lies outside them all goes to Outside.

params.label: Attributes to fetch
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: From the area of Overlay each part lies in. Empty fetches all

params.label: Prefix
params.hint: Put in front of the fetched names, for example zone_. Without it, a name the features already have is not fetched

node_types.title: Find nearest
node_types.description: Finds for each feature in Base the nearest feature in Candidates, and gives it the distance and the attributes of that one. Features with nothing within the largest distance go to Unmatched.

params.label: Largest distance
params.hint: Features with nothing this near go to Unmatched. Empty looks as far as it takes. In the units of the coordinate system

params.label: Distance attribute
params.hint: The distance to the nearest one

params.label: Attributes to fetch
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: From the nearest candidate. Empty fetches all

params.label: Prefix
params.hint: Put in front of the fetched names, for example near_. Without it, a name the features already have is not fetched

node_types.title: Split lines
node_types.description: Splits lines where points lie on them, where they cross or meet each other, or both. Each part keeps the attributes of its line.

params.label: Split at
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: The points connected to Points, the places where lines cross or meet each other, or both

params.label: Tolerance
params.hint: How far from a line a point may be and still split it, in the units of the coordinate system

params.label: Part number
params.shape: the name of an attribute to add, or empty for none
params.hint: Numbers the parts of each line from 1, in the order along the line

node_types.title: Overlay areas
node_types.description: Lays two sets of areas over each other. Where they overlap, the part gets the attributes of both and goes to Both. What is left of each goes to Areas only and Overlay only.

params.label: Attributes to fetch
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: From the Overlay areas, for the parts in Both. Empty fetches all

params.label: Prefix
params.hint: Put in front of the fetched names. Without it, a name the Areas already have is not fetched

node_types.title: Clip
node_types.description: Clips points, lines and areas against the clip areas. Lines and areas are split at the boundary. Points exactly on the boundary count as inside. All clip areas are merged into one before clipping. Heights are kept: a new corner gets its height from the edge or the plane it was cut from. 3D models, such as a TIN, a surface or buildings, are cut from above, each triangle in its own plane, and walls by upright planes along the boundary.

params.label: 3D models along the edge
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: A building or another solid cut by the edge is closed with a new wall there, on each side, so that it stands whole in a 3D print or a picture

node_types.title: Dissolve
node_types.description: Merges areas that touch or overlap, in each group. Shared boundaries disappear and overlaps count once. Areas that do not touch stay features of their own, or become one multi-area for each group as a choice. Only the group-by attributes are kept. Features that are not areas go to Remnants.

params.label: Group by
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Only areas with the same values are merged. Empty merges all that touch

params.label: Count attribute
params.hint: The number of areas that were merged

params.label: Areas apart
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Each a feature of its own

params.hint: What is left apart after merging, such as buildings that do not touch

node_types.title: Count points in polygons
node_types.description: Counts the points in each polygon and writes the number to an attribute of the polygon. A point on a boundary counts as inside.

params.label: Count attribute
params.hint: The number of points in each polygon. An attribute that already exists is overwritten

node_types.title: Join by location
node_types.description: A spatial join, as Join attributes by location in QGIS: gives each feature the attributes of the features in Join it lies within, crosses, touches or is near: points, lines and areas in both. Each point the municipality it is in, each road the zones it crosses, each stop the nearest line. One, every one, or summarized. Features that find nothing go to Unjoined.

params.label: Features that
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Touch or overlap in any way
Have their point inside (one per feature)

params.hint: How a feature is to lie to a feature in Join to get its attributes. Within: a feature in Features lies within one in Join. Their point inside is how Join by location worked before 0.77: a line or an area is placed by one point on it

params.label: Distance
params.hint: For Lie within a distance: how near, in the units of the coordinate system

params.label: When several are found
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Every one: a feature for each
Summarized: count, and the values together

params.hint: Summarized keeps every feature in Joined, those that found nothing with the count 0

params.label: Summarize numbers as
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Text is always listed, each value once, separated by commas

params.label: Count attribute
params.hint: When summarized: how many were found

params.label: Attributes to fetch
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: From the features in Join that are found. Empty fetches all

params.label: Prefix
params.hint: Put in front of the fetched names, for example area_. Without it, a name the features already have is not fetched

node_types.title: Overlay points on areas
node_types.description: Replaced by Join by location and Count points in polygons. Each point gets the attributes of the area it lies in, and each area the number of points in it.

params.label: Count attribute
params.hint: Areas found for a point, and points found in an area

node_types.title: Extend lines
node_types.description: Makes lines longer at one or both ends, straight on in the direction of the end, by a distance in the units of the coordinate system.

params.label: Distance
params.hint: In the units of the coordinate system, such as metres in SWEREF 99 TM

params.label: At
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Each end goes on in the direction of its last piece

node_types.title: Snap
node_types.description: Moves the points of the features that lie within a distance of the features on Fixed, which stay as they are: to their nearest point, or to the nearest place on their lines and edges. Without Fixed, the features snap to each other.

params.label: Largest distance
params.hint: Points closer than this are moved. In the units of the coordinate system, such as metres

params.label: Snap to
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The nearest point of a line or area
The nearest place on a line or edge

params.hint: With Fixed connected. Without it, the features snap to each other's points, and the first ones stay where they are

node_types.title: Buffer
node_types.description: Replaces each geometry with the area within a distance of it. Points become discs, lines corridors, and areas grow, or shrink with a negative distance. Lines can be buffered on one side only, left or right as they are drawn, and with flat ends. Works in metres.

params.label: Distance
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: In metres. A number, or an expression such as width / 2. Negative shrinks areas

params.label: Side
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Of lines: one side only, left or right as the line is drawn, such as the land along one bank of a river. Areas and points get buffers all round

params.label: Ends of lines
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Flat ends stop where the line stops

node_types.title: Remove holes
node_types.description: Fills the holes of areas: all of them, or those smaller than a size, such as the courtyards of blocks or small clearings in a forest.

params.label: Holes smaller than
params.hint: In square metres: holes smaller than this are filled, larger ones kept. Empty fills every hole

node_types.title: Round shapes
node_types.description: Rounds areas as in a drawing for children or a game map: every corner becomes a curve of the radius, narrow gaps and inlets are filled and narrow spits and points cut away. Parts and holes smaller than a size you give go. Works in metres; lines and points are passed on as they are.

params.label: Radius in metres
params.hint: Corners become curves of this radius, and inlets, gaps and spits narrower than twice it go

params.label: Smallest part in m²
params.hint: Parts and holes smaller go. Empty: keep all

node_types.title: Replace with center point
node_types.description: Replaces each geometry with a single point: its centre of mass, a point guaranteed to lie inside it, or the centre of its bounding box.

params.label: Point
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: The centre of mass can fall outside a curved shape. A point inside never does

node_types.title: Generalize
node_types.description: Simplifies lines and area boundaries by removing vertices that change the shape by less than the tolerance (Douglas–Peucker). Points are left as they are.

params.label: Tolerance
params.hint: In the units of the coordinate system, normally metres. Vertices closer than this to the simplified line are removed

params.label: Keep neighbours together
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: A boundary that two areas share is simplified once, so that no gaps or overlaps arise. The areas must share their vertices along it

node_types.title: Every pair
node_types.description: Pairs every feature of From with every one of To, or with those within a distance: the origins and destinations of a matrix of travel times. Each pair has the attributes of both, the coordinates of both for a route planner such as OpenTripPlanner, and a line between them.

params.label: Largest distance
params.hint: Only pairs this near each other, in the units of the coordinate system. Empty pairs every one with every one

params.label: Geometry of a pair
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: A line from one to the other

params.label: Prefix of To
params.hint: Put in front of the names of the attributes of To, so that they are not mixed up with those of From

params.label: Coordinates as attributes in
params.hint: from_lat, from_lon, to_lat and to_lon in WGS 84, as OpenTripPlanner and other route planners want them. Empty leaves them out

params.label: Leave out a feature paired with itself
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: When the same stream comes to both, as for travel times between all stops

node_types.title: Split lines into segments
node_types.description: Explodes each line into its segments: a line from each corner to the next, with the attributes of the line and which segment it is. The outlines of areas can be split too; points pass as they are.

params.label: Areas
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Number attribute
params.hint: Which segment of its line each is, from 1. Empty leaves it out

node_types.title: Convex hull
node_types.description: The smallest convex area around each feature, or around all of them or each group together, as a rubber band stretched around them. Points in a row give a line.

params.label: A hull around
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Group by
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: All together: one hull for each group of features with the same values. Empty gives one around all

params.label: Count attribute
params.hint: All together: how many features each hull holds. Empty leaves it out

node_types.title: Concave hull
node_types.description: An area around points, or the corners of lines and areas, that follows them inwards where they leave room: the shape of a spread of points rather than the rubber band around them. Concavity says how tightly.

params.label: A hull around
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Group by
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: All together: one hull for each group of features with the same values. Empty gives one around all

params.label: Count attribute
params.hint: All together: how many features each hull holds. Empty leaves it out

params.label: Concavity
params.hint: Lower follows the points more tightly: 0.5 is close, 2 rough, and 10 or more nearly the convex hull

params.label: Shortest edge
params.hint: Edges shorter than this are not cut into further, in the units of the coordinate system. 0 cuts all

node_types.title: Aggregate
node_types.description: Joins features into one multi-geometry, all of them or one per group. The geometries are kept as they are; to merge areas into one, use Dissolve.

params.label: Group by
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Features with the same values become one. Empty puts all in one

params.label: Count attribute
params.hint: An attribute with the number of features each one was made of, for example count. Empty adds none

node_types.title: Deaggregate
node_types.description: Splits multi-geometries into their parts, each a feature of its own with the attributes of the whole.

params.label: Part number attribute
params.hint: The number of the part within the feature it came from, 1, 2 and so on. Empty adds none

node_types.title: Create points from x and y
node_types.description: Makes a point of each feature from two attributes with its x and y. Features where either is missing or not a number go to Failed.

params.label: x attribute
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: East, or longitude

params.label: y attribute
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: North, or latitude

params.label: Coordinate system
params.hint: Of the x and y values, for example EPSG:3006 for SWEREF 99 TM or EPSG:4326 for degrees. Empty keeps the one the stream has

node_types.title: Geometry to text
node_types.description: Writes the geometry of each feature as text in an attribute: WKT, EWKT with the coordinate system in front, or GeoJSON, with heights where it has them and as many decimals as you want. For a web service, a database or a sheet. The geometry can be kept or dropped.

params.label: As
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Attribute
params.hint: The attribute that gets the text

params.label: Decimals
params.hint: Of the coordinates, such as 2 for centimetres in metres. Empty: as they are

params.label: Heights
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: With Z where the geometry has heights, as POINT Z (1 2 3)

params.label: Keep the geometry
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Geometry from text
node_types.description: Makes geometry of text in an attribute, as web services give it: WKT (also with SRID= in front and with Z), GeoJSON and Esri JSON from ArcGIS. The coordinate system is the one you choose, or the one the text names. Text that cannot be read goes to Failed.

params.label: Geometry in
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute with the geometry as text, such as Geometry.SWEREF99TM from Trafikverket or geometry from an API

params.label: Written as
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: As the text is: WKT, GeoJSON or Esri JSON
Encoded polyline, as routes from OpenTripPlanner and OSRM
Encoded polyline with 6 decimals, as from Valhalla
Flexible polyline, as routes from HERE
Flexible polyline as an area, as isolines from HERE
A JSON list of points, as a route from TomTom: a line
A JSON list of points as an area, as a reachable range from TomTom

params.label: Coordinate system
params.hint: Of the coordinates in the text. Empty: as the text says (SRID=, spatialReference), WGS 84 for GeoJSON, or else none

params.label: Keep the text attribute
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Points to lines
node_types.description: Joins points into lines, one for each value of an attribute, in the order of another: the shapes of GTFS, a GPS track, a way from Overpass. Can close each line into an area. Heights go along.

params.label: One line for each
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute that says which line a point belongs to, such as shape_id in GTFS or a track id. Empty makes one line of all points

params.label: In the order of
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Such as shape_pt_sequence or a time. Empty keeps the order they come in

params.label: Close each line into an area
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Replace with bounding box
node_types.description: Replaces each geometry with the smallest rectangle around it, along the axes. A box without width or height becomes a line or a point.

params.label: Add the corners as attributes
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Yes: xmin, ymin, xmax and ymax

node_types.title: Bounding box of all
node_types.description: One rectangle around all the features of the stream, or one for each group, with a count of the features in it.

params.label: Group by
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: One box for each group of features with the same values. Empty gives one box around all

params.label: Count attribute
params.hint: How many features are in each box. Empty leaves it out

params.label: Add the corners as attributes
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Yes: xmin, ymin, xmax and ymax

node_types.title: Polygons to lines
node_types.description: Turns each area into its boundary as lines: the outer ring and the rings of the holes. What is not an area goes to Other.

node_types.title: Lines to polygons
node_types.description: Turns closed lines into areas. The parts of a line that meet end to end are joined into a ring first. Lines whose ends do not meet go to Failed.

params.label: Ends that meet within
params.hint: In the units of the coordinate system. Ends this close count as one point, so that a line that almost closes becomes an area

node_types.title: Thiessen polygons
node_types.description: Gives each point the area that lies nearer to it than to any other point (Thiessen or Voronoi polygons), with the attributes of the point. Areas connected to Boundary cut them, otherwise a box around the points does.

params.label: Margin in %
params.hint: How far the outer areas reach beyond the points, as a share of the larger side of the area the points cover. Not used when areas are connected to Boundary

node_types.title: Create features
node_types.description: Makes points, lines or areas from coordinates you write, a feature on each line, or from WKT and GeoJSON: a place to start from, a study area to clip by, or a few points to test a model with. Each gets a number and, if you give them, a name.

params.label: Make
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: As WKT or GeoJSON, one on each line

params.label: Coordinates
params.shape: text over several lines, such as SQL, with {attribute} put in from the stream on the port
params.hint: A feature on each line: x and y after each other, such as 319500 6399700 for a point, or 319500 6399700, 320100 6400200 for a line. An area is closed by itself. Or WKT, such as POINT(319500 6399700)

params.label: Names
params.hint: Put in the attribute name, separated by commas, one for each feature in order

node_types.title: Create grid
node_types.description: Makes a grid of squares or hexagons over the features that come in on Extent: all cells in their extent, or the ones that touch them. Each cell is numbered, with its row and column.

params.label: Shape
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Size
params.hint: The side of a square, or the width of a hexagon from side to side, in the units of the coordinate system

params.label: Keep
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Start at whole sizes
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Lines up the grid with multiples of the size, so that grids made from different data fit together

node_types.title: Remove geometry
node_types.description: Takes away the geometry and keeps the attributes, so that the stream is a plain table.

node_types.title: Set coordinate system
node_types.description: Says which coordinate system the stream is in, without changing the coordinates. For data that lacks one, or states the wrong one.

params.label: Coordinate system
params.hint: As an EPSG code, for example EPSG:3006 for SWEREF 99 TM. The coordinates are not changed: use Reproject for that

node_types.title: Geometry to 2D
node_types.description: Makes the geometry two-dimensional: the heights (Z) of the coordinates go, and the 3D model that comes with a stream, such as from an IFC, CityGML or OBJ file, so that what is left is the plan, shown and written in 2D. Measures (M) are dropped when data is read.

node_types.title: Scale
node_types.description: Makes the geometry larger or smaller by a factor, around the origin or the middle of the features. For example 0.001 to turn CAD drawings in millimetres into metres.

params.label: Factor
params.hint: 1000 makes the geometry a thousand times larger. 0.001 turns millimetres into metres

params.label: Factor in y
params.hint: Empty is the same as the factor

params.label: Around
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The origin, 0 0 in the coordinate system
The middle of all features together

params.hint: The point that stays where it is

params.label: Heights
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: For data with Z and 3D models. Scaled from 0, or from the lowest point when scaled around a middle, so that what stands on the ground stays there

node_types.title: Move by x, y and z
node_types.description: Moves the geometry a distance along x and along y, in the units of the stream's coordinate system, and up or down: features with Z, 3D models and grids of heights.

params.label: Along x
params.hint: In the units of the stream's coordinate system, such as metres in SWEREF 99 TM. Negative moves west

params.label: Along y
params.hint: Negative moves south

params.label: Up
params.hint: Moves heights: of features with Z, of 3D models and of a grid of heights. Negative moves down

node_types.title: Rotate
node_types.description: Turns the geometry by an angle in degrees, counter-clockwise, around the middle of each feature, the middle of all of them or a point you give. The angle can come from an attribute. Heights stay as they are, and a 3D model turns with its features.

params.label: Angle, in degrees
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: Counter-clockwise; negative turns clockwise. A number, or an expression such as an attribute with the angle of each feature

params.label: Around
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The middle of all features together

params.hint: The point that stays where it is

params.label: Point, x
params.hint: In the coordinate system of the stream

node_types.title: Swap x and y
node_types.description: Swaps the x and y coordinates of all geometry, for data where they have been mixed up: latitude given as x, or northing and easting in the wrong order. Heights stay as they are. Lines and areas are swapped too.

node_types.title: Reverse geometry
node_types.description: Turns the direction of lines and of the outlines of areas, holes too, so that they start where they ended, with their heights: clockwise becomes counter-clockwise. The parts of a multi geometry come in the opposite order. Areas can be kept as they are; points stay as they are.

params.label: Areas
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: The outline of an area runs one way round. Some formats want it clockwise, others not

node_types.title: Reproject
node_types.description: Reprojects the geometry to another coordinate system. The axis order is always east, north.

params.label: Cell size of a raster
params.hint: A raster gets cells of this size in the new system. Empty keeps about the size it had

node_types.title: Set height
node_types.description: Gives every coordinate of each feature a height (Z): from an attribute or an expression, such as the height of a contour line; from the terrain model connected to Terrain, such as roads laid on the ground; or the heights they have and a value more. Can make them flat again. The heights are kept by tools that do not change the geometry, shown in 3D on the map and written to formats that take them.

params.label: Height
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: From the value below: all coordinates at that height
From the terrain model on Terrain, plus the value below
The heights they have, plus the value below
Take the heights away: flat again

params.label: Value
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: An attribute, such as the height of a contour line, a number, or an expression such as floors * 3. Empty is 0

node_types.title: Check geometry
node_types.description: Finds geometries that are not valid, such as areas whose boundary crosses itself, and says what is wrong. They can be repaired: the repaired ones go to Repaired and those that cannot be go to Invalid. Features without geometry are Invalid.

params.label: Repair what is wrong
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Repaired features go to Repaired, as GDAL makes them valid. Those that cannot be repaired go to Invalid

params.label: Problem attribute
params.hint: What was wrong, on Invalid and Repaired

node_types.title: Extract coordinates from point
node_types.description: Puts the x and y of each point in attributes of their own. Lines and areas give a point inside them, their centre or their first point.

params.label: Attribute for x
params.hint: East, or longitude in degrees

params.label: Attribute for y
params.hint: North, or latitude in degrees

params.label: Decimals
params.hint: Rounds the coordinates, such as 0 for whole metres or 6 for degrees. Empty keeps them as they are

params.label: For lines and areas
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Filter by geometry type
node_types.description: Sends points, lines and areas to an output each. The cells of a raster go to Raster, and features without geometry to Other. The points of a point cloud go to Point: to take its ground or buildings out, use Filter by value or Test on classification.

node_types.title: Filter 2D/3D
node_types.description: Sends features with heights to 3D and flat ones to 2D: geometry with a height for each coordinate, as read with Z or given heights with Set height, and the objects of a 3D model, which keep their part of the model. Features without geometry go to No geometry.

node_types.title: Calculate area
node_types.description: Writes the area to an attribute. In metre-based systems the area is planar, in degrees it is geodesic on the ellipsoid.

params.label: Unit
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Decimals
params.hint: Rounds to this many decimals. Empty keeps them all

node_types.title: Calculate length
node_types.description: Writes the length of a line, or the perimeter of an area, to an attribute.

params.label: Unit
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Decimals
params.hint: Rounds to this many decimals. Empty keeps them all

node_types.title: STAC search
node_types.description: Finds satellite images, aerial photos and height models in a STAC catalogue, such as those of Lantmäteriet, Copernicus or Element 84: in an area, at a time, in chosen collections. Each item becomes its outline, with its date, its cloud cover and the address of each of its files, which Input can read.

params.label: STAC API
params.hint: The address of the catalogue, such as https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1. /search is added

params.label: Collections
params.hint: Such as sentinel-2-l2a. Several are separated by commas. Empty searches all

params.label: Time
params.hint: A date, month or year, or from and to: 2026-06-01/2026-08-31 or 2026-06/2026-08. Empty: any time

params.label: Area, in WGS 84
params.hint: west, south, east, north in degrees, such as 11.8, 57.6, 12.1, 57.8. A stream on Area is used instead, if one is connected

params.label: Filter
params.hint: A CQL2 filter the catalogue understands, such as eo:cloud_cover < 20

params.label: API connection
params.shape: the name of an API connection in the settings of the user
params.hint: For a catalogue that needs a login, such as Lantmäteriet's

node_types.title: HTTP request
node_types.description: Sends a request for each feature that comes in, or one request when nothing is connected to Input, and puts the answer in an attribute, for example JSON from an API or a web page. GET, or POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE with a body. Those that get no good answer go to Failed.

params.label: Address
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: A web address, or an expression that builds one from the attributes: 'https://api.example.org/item?id=' || id

params.label: Method
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: GET asks for something; POST and PUT send something along

params.label: Body
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: What is sent with POST, PUT or PATCH: an attribute such as json from Build JSON, or an expression. Empty sends nothing

params.label: Content type
params.hint: What the body is, sent as the header Content-Type

params.label: Headers
params.hint: For example Accept: application/json. Several are separated by ;

params.label: Response attribute
params.hint: The answer, as text

params.label: Status attribute
params.hint: The status code of the answer, such as 200 or 404

params.label: Timeout in seconds
params.hint: How long to wait for each answer

params.label: API connection
params.shape: the name of an API connection in the settings of the user
params.hint: The key, user or OAuth2 client, kept in the settings and not in the model. Where the key goes in the address or the body, write {{key}}

params.label: Pages
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: A link to the next page

params.hint: For an answer that comes in pages: each page becomes a feature, with its number in _page

params.label: Next page at
params.hint: The path to the address of the next page, such as next_page, links[rel=next].href or @odata.nextLink. Empty uses the Link header

params.label: Parameter of the page
params.hint: Such as offset, skip, start or page

params.label: Parameter of the page size
params.hint: Such as limit, per_page or pageSize. Empty sends no size

params.label: Page size
params.hint: How many items a page holds

params.label: First value
params.hint: Where counting starts: 0 for an offset, 1 for a page number, if empty

params.label: Items at
params.hint: The path to the list of items in a page, such as values or features, to know when the pages end. Empty takes the first list

params.label: At most pages
params.hint: A stop, should the pages never end

params.label: At most requests a second
params.hint: As a service asks, such as 1 for Nominatim. Empty sends them as fast as the answers come

params.label: The answer
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: As a file, its path in _file

params.hint: A file for answers that are not text, such as a GeoTIFF of travel times. Read the files with an Input, with this stream connected to its Paths

params.label: Folder for the files
params.hint: Beside the model, or a whole path. Each file is named by its request, so the same request gives the same file

params.label: Requests at once
params.hint: Sends this many at the same time, such as 8 to a service of your own, such as OpenTripPlanner. A public service wants 1

params.label: Keep the answers
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Yes, in a folder beside the model

params.hint: Good answers are kept in the folder http-cache beside the model, and the same request is not sent again in later runs. Delete the folder to ask anew

params.label: Write every request to
params.shape: a file to write; relative paths start at the folder of the model
params.hint: A text file, such as requests.log, with a line for each request: when, the method, the address, the status, the size and time of the answer, and the body sent. Added to in each run. Secrets of the API connection are hidden. Empty: none

params.label: Tries again
params.hint: When the service is busy (429), briefly away (502, 503, 504) or cannot be reached: waits as the service says, or 1, 2, 4… seconds

node_types.title: Flatten JSON
node_types.description: Makes the JSON in an attribute into attributes of their own, so that the stream is a plain table: {"adress": {"ort": "Borås"}} gives adress.ort. Lists are kept as JSON text, or get an attribute per element. Features whose attribute is not JSON go to Failed.

params.label: JSON in
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute with JSON text, such as the answer from HTTP request or an object that an input kept as JSON

params.label: Lists
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: As JSON text in one attribute
An attribute per element: name.0, name.1, …

params.hint: For a feature per element, use Explode JSON list

params.label: Prefix
params.hint: Put before the new names, such as svar. Empty uses the names in the JSON, and a name the stream has already gets the name of the attribute in front

params.label: Keep the JSON attribute
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Explode JSON list
node_types.description: Makes a feature of each element of a list in JSON, with the attributes of the feature it came from and the values of the element, such as one feature per clinic of a hospital. Features without a list, or with an empty one, go to Other.

params.label: JSON in
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute with the list, or with JSON that holds it

params.label: List at
params.hint: Where the list is in the JSON, such as mottagningar or data.items. Empty: the attribute is the list. Several lists of the same length, separated by commas, are taken in step: hourly.time, hourly.temperature_2m

params.label: Prefix
params.hint: Put before the names of the values of each element. Empty uses the names in the JSON, and a name the stream has already gets the name of the list in front

params.label: Number the elements
params.shape: the name of an attribute to add, or empty for none
params.hint: The place of each element in its list, from 0, in an attribute

params.label: Keep the JSON attribute
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Extract JSON values
node_types.description: Takes chosen values out of the JSON in an attribute, each by its path, such as adress.ort or kontakter[0].telefon, into attributes. A value that is not there is left empty. Features whose attribute is not JSON go to Failed.

params.label: JSON in
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute with JSON text

params.label: Values to take
params.shape: a list of [path in the JSON, attribute name]
params.hint: A path and the attribute it goes to, such as adress.ort or kontakter[0].telefon. An empty name takes the last part of the path. An object or a list is taken as JSON text

node_types.title: Extract XML values
node_types.description: Takes chosen values out of the XML in an attribute, such as the answer of a web service, each by its path of element names, such as Fastighet.Adress.Ort or Fastighet.Tel[1], into attributes. An XML attribute is taken by its name. A value that is not there is left empty. Features whose attribute is not XML go to Failed.

params.label: XML in
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute with XML text, such as the answer of a web service

params.label: Values to take
params.shape: a list of [path in the JSON, attribute name]
params.hint: A path of element names and the attribute it goes to, such as Fastighet.Adress.Ort or Fastighet.Tel[1], from the outermost element. An XML attribute is taken by its name, as Fastighet.id. An empty name takes the last part of the path

node_types.title: JSON-stat to table
node_types.description: Makes a table of statistics in JSON-stat, as SCB (PxWeb), Eurostat, Folkhälsomyndigheten and other statistics agencies give them: a row for each value with the code and the name of each category, such as region, sex and year, or with the categories of one dimension as columns. Answers that are not JSON-stat go to Failed.

params.label: JSON-stat in

params.hint: The attribute with the answer from SCB, Eurostat or another service that gives JSON-stat, such as _response from HTTP request

params.label: Names of the categories
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Such as Borås next to 1490, in Region_label

params.label: Columns from
params.hint: A dimension whose categories become columns, such as Tid for a column per year or ContentsCode for one per measure. Empty gives a row per value

params.label: Values that are missing
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Build JSON
node_types.description: Writes attributes as a JSON object in an attribute of its own: all of them or the ones chosen, names with a dot as nested objects, and the geometry as GeoJSON if you want it. For sending on to a web service, or for writing as text.

params.label: Attributes
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: The attributes to put in. Empty puts in all of them

params.label: Write to
params.hint: The attribute that gets the JSON text

params.label: Make
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: One list of all the features
A list for each value of an attribute

params.hint: A list gathers the objects of the features, all of them or those with the same value, into one feature each, as a web service wants a list of many

params.label: Lists by

params.hint: The attribute whose values each get a list. The list's feature keeps the value

params.label: List under the name
params.hint: Puts the list in an object under this name, such as {"features": [...]}. Empty writes the list as it is

params.label: Names with a dot as objects
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: adress.gata and adress.ort become "adress": {"gata": …, "ort": …}, as Flatten JSON took them apart

params.label: JSON text as JSON
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: An attribute that holds a JSON object or list is put in as such, not as text

params.label: Geometry
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: In the coordinates of the stream

params.label: Over several lines
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Easier to read, longer

node_types.title: Draw map
node_types.description: Draws the streams connected to Layers into a picture with coordinates: each stream a layer with its own colours, in the order you set, with values shown by colour and size, labels, icons for points, and a legend. Write the picture to PNG, JPG, GeoTIFF or PDF with an output.

params.label: Layers

params.hint: Each stream connected to Layers is a layer. The top row is drawn on top

params.label: Size
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: For print: width in mm and pixels to the inch

params.label: Pixels to the inch

params.label: Style

params.label: Margin in %

params.label: Background

choices.label: A background map, such as OpenStreetMap

params.label: Background map

choices.label: One of my own, or an address

params.label: Paler by %

params.label: Legend
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Scale bar

params.label: North arrow

params.label: Grid

params.label: Grid every

params.label: Overview map

node_types.title: Draw chart

The chart comes out as a picture to write to a .png or a .pdf, and can also be written as an interactive web page, where each value shows under the pointer and the bars can be sorted.

node_types.title: Render 3D scene
node_types.description: The picture of a 3D scene for presenting: models such as buildings read from OBJ, glTF, 3D Tiles or IFC, or made with Extrude or Generate TIN, rendered by following rays of light: lit by the sun, with soft shadows, and by the sky, which reaches into the shade and darkens corners, with their materials, textures and glass. On a light floor, under the sky as it is at that hour, or on the terrain connected to Terrain with the map on Map laid over it. Clouds, haze, water that mirrors, reflections and more bounces of the light, or the models white or in wood as a model. At dusk, lit windows, lamps at the points on Lights and materials that glow; depth of field blurs what is not in focus. The sun can stand where it does on a date and at a time, and a sun study gives a sheet of pictures through the day. A picture can take some minutes. For a quick look at terrain alone, use Quick terrain view.

The kinds of land, such as forest, fields and towns, lie on it as thin plates in clear or pastel colours, picked by the words in their names in Swedish or English, or as you give them. The largest kind is the ground. Trees stand in the forest, pines where it is coniferous, houses with bright roofs in towns, animals of many kinds graze on fields and meadows, play in towns and roam the forest, sailing boats lie on the water, and fluffy clouds float above, all casting their shadows. The board can be round. Render it with parallel projection, no floor and a see-through background for a picture like a diorama. The pieces come out as areas with their layer, kind, colour and heights.
