params.hint: Metres inside the footprint, so that walls, eaves and trees at the edge do not count

params.label: Roofs
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The shape that fits the points best: flat, shed, gable or hipped
All flat, at the height of the roof

params.label: Walls
params.hint: A colour, such as #e8e0d0

params.label: Roofs coloured
params.hint: A colour, such as #9a4b3c for tiles or #555555 for felt

node_types.title: Terrain to 3D model
node_types.description: Makes the heights of a raster on Heights into a 3D model of the terrain: a surface of triangles, with a picture on Picture, such as an orthophoto or a map from Draw map, draped over it. With a block under it if you like, to print or to set on a table. For glTF and Blender, the 3D view and Render 3D scene.

params.label: Points along a side
params.hint: At most this many points of height along the longer side: more is finer and larger. Cells are skipped to keep to it

params.label: Heights times
params.hint: Such as 2 to make hills twice as high

params.label: Base
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: A block under it, with sides and a bottom, to print or set on a table

params.label: Block below the lowest
params.hint: In metres. Empty: a tenth of the height of the terrain, at least 1

params.label: Largest picture
params.hint: Pixels along a side of the picture draped over the terrain; larger is made smaller

node_types.title: Make buildings
node_types.description: Makes buildings that look like buildings from their footprints on Buildings: as high as their height or storeys, with the roof their attributes give (flat, shed, gable or hipped), facades with a window in every bay of every storey, and the colours and materials of their kind: plaster for houses, glass for offices and shops, sheet metal for industry, stone for churches and plain walls for garages. The attributes of OpenStreetMap (building, building:levels, height, roof:shape, roof:height, roof:orientation, building:colour, roof:material), Overture (class, num_floors, roof_shape) and the property map (objekttyp) are recognised by themselves. They stand on the terrain on Terrain, or at 0. For the 3D view, Render 3D scene, glTF and the walk-through.

params.label: Kind by
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: What the building is, such as house, apartments, office, industrial, church or garage, or Bostad and Industri. Empty: building, class or objekttyp, whichever there is

params.label: Height by
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The height to the top of the roof in metres. Empty: height, if there is one; else from the storeys

params.label: Storeys by
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The number of storeys below the roof. Empty: building:levels, num_floors or levels, whichever there is

params.label: Roof shape by
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: flat, skillion, gabled, hipped, pyramidal and the other shapes of OpenStreetMap. Empty: roof:shape or roof_shape

params.label: Storeys when not known
params.hint: For buildings with neither a height nor storeys

params.label: Height of a storey
params.hint: In metres, from floor to floor

params.label: Roof when not known
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Gable on houses of up to three storeys and small buildings, else flat

params.hint: For buildings whose roof shape is not given

params.label: Pitch of the roofs
params.hint: In degrees, for sloping roofs whose height is not given

params.label: Windows
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Facades with a row of windows on each storey, as a texture. No: plain walls in the colours of their kind

node_types.title: Lighten 3D model
node_types.description: Makes a 3D model lighter, to be shown in realtime in a browser, a game engine or on a phone: fewer triangles where they show little, by meshoptimizer, to a number of triangles or a largest change in metres, with the edges of each object kept; textures no larger than needed; and the plain colours and textures put together into one texture, an atlas, so that the model is drawn in few calls. Each object keeps its attributes. Write it as glTF with the compression of meshoptimizer, as 3D Tiles or as a walk-through.

params.label: Triangles at most
params.hint: In all, shared among the objects by how many they have. Empty: as few as Largest change allows

params.label: Largest change
params.hint: How far in metres the surface may move, such as 0.5. Empty: as far as it must to reach the number of triangles

params.label: Keep the edges
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: The edges of each object and material stay where they are, so that the pieces still meet without gaps

params.label: Largest texture
params.hint: In pixels on the longer side; larger textures are made smaller. Empty: as they are

params.label: One texture for the materials
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Plain colours and textures that do not repeat go into one texture, an atlas, so that the model is drawn in few calls. Textures that repeat, such as facades, and glass keep their own

node_types.title: Overture Maps download
node_types.description: Fetches open map data from Overture Maps: buildings with their heights, places such as shops and schools with their categories, addresses, roads and paths, land use, water, and the borders of countries and municipalities. Only what reaches into a rectangle, or the extent of what comes in on Extent, is fetched, by reading only the parts of the large files on the web that hold it. Needs the internet.

params.label: What
params.shape: some of the values in choices: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas

choices.label: Places: shops, schools, restaurants and more
Land: forests, rocks, islands and more
Infrastructure: bridges, towers, power lines and more
Areas of countries, regions and municipalities

params.hint: Tick one or more. Each feature gets the attribute kind, such as buildings/building

params.label: Rectangle
params.hint: West, south, east, north in degrees, such as 11.95, 57.69, 11.99, 57.71. Not needed when something comes in on Extent

params.label: Largest area in km²
params.hint: A larger rectangle is made smaller around its middle to this size. The files are large, and each part of one that reaches into the rectangle is fetched

params.label: Large features
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Cut at the edge of the area
Whole, when they reach into the area

params.hint: Land cover, land use, water and borders can be very large: cut, only the part within the area comes along

params.label: Coordinate system
params.hint: Of what comes out. Overture Maps is in WGS 84

params.label: Release
params.hint: Such as 2026-10-21.0. Empty takes the latest; a release is kept for a few months

params.label: Catalog
params.hint: Where the catalog of the releases is

node_types.title: Values from raster
node_types.description: Gives each feature the value of the raster where it lies: the height of the terrain at each address, the land cover under each tree, the noise at each school. The value of the cell, or between the four nearest cells for heights. A line or an area gets the value at a point on it; Zonal statistics gives the mean and more over each area.

params.label: Attribute
params.hint: Gets the value. A raster with several bands gives name_2, name_3 and so on too

params.label: Value
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Between the four nearest cells (bilinear), for heights and other smooth values

params.hint: The cell it lies in suits classes, such as land cover

node_types.title: Zonal statistics
node_types.description: Counts the cells of the raster within each area: how many, the mean, the smallest and largest, sum, median, spread and the most common value, and for classes, such as land cover, the share or area of each. A cell counts when its middle lies in the area. The share of forest in each municipality, the mean height of each property, the people in each district from a population grid. A series of pictures over time, such as from Read satellite bands, gives each area a row for each time, with the time: the NDVI of each field through a summer.

params.label: Statistics
params.hint: Any of count, mean, min, max, sum, median, std, range, majority and area, separated by commas

params.label: Each value apart
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The share of each value, in percent

params.hint: For classes, such as land cover: an attribute for each value, such as share_3 for the share of the cells with 3

params.label: Before the names
params.hint: Such as dem_, to give dem_mean and dem_max

node_types.title: Slope and aspect
node_types.description: Measures the terrain from a grid of heights, cell by cell: the slope in degrees or percent, the aspect (which way it faces), the position against the surroundings, which picks out ridges and valleys (TPI), or the roughness.

params.label: Measure
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Aspect: the way the slope faces, degrees from north
Position: above or below the surroundings (TPI)
Roughness: the largest difference to a neighbour

params.label: Surroundings
params.hint: For the position: how many cells out the surroundings reach. Ridges and valleys show at about their width

params.label: Heights times
params.hint: When the heights are in other units than the coordinates, such as feet on metres: 0.3048

node_types.title: Clip raster
node_types.description: Keeps the cells of a raster inside the areas on Areas, or outside them, and cuts the raster to them. A grid of values or a picture. To reproject a raster, use Reproject.

params.label: Keep the cells
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: A cell is inside when its middle is

params.label: The raster
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Keep the size of the raster

node_types.title: Raster to areas
node_types.description: Makes areas of the cells with the same value that touch, with the value as an attribute: land cover, zones of noise or of a viewshed as polygons. For a raster of measures, such as heights, make classes first with Reclassify raster.

params.label: Attribute
params.hint: The value of the cells of each area

params.label: Cells belong together
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Cells with the same value that touch become one area

params.label: Areas
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Features to raster
node_types.description: Makes a raster of features: each cell gets the value of the area its middle lies in, the line that passes through it or the point in it. A value from an attribute or expression, or how many features. The cells are of a size, or those of a raster connected to Like, so that it can be counted with that one.

params.label: Value
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: The value of the cells of each feature: a number, an attribute or an expression

params.label: Cell size
params.hint: In the units of the coordinate system, such as metres. A raster connected to Like gives its cells instead

params.label: Where several features are
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Other cells
params.hint: The value of cells no feature reaches. Empty leaves them empty

node_types.title: Reclassify raster
node_types.description: Gives the cells new values by ranges: heights into bands, slopes into classes, land cover codes into groups. From, to and the new value, the first range that fits.

params.label: From, to and new value
params.shape: a list of [from, to, value]; an empty from or to has no end
params.hint: From and to are both in the range, and the first range that fits is used: 0 to 5 gives 1, 5 to 15 gives 2. An empty from or to has no end

params.label: Values in no range
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Distance raster
node_types.description: A raster of the distance from each cell to the nearest feature, as far as a distance: to the nearest road, school, shore or stop. Exact from the middle of the cells, in the units of the coordinate system.

params.label: Cell size
params.hint: In the units of the coordinate system, such as metres. A raster connected to Like gives its cells instead

params.label: As far as
params.hint: How far from the features the raster reaches; cells farther away are empty

node_types.title: Visible area
node_types.description: What can be seen from places on the terrain (a viewshed): for each cell, how many of the places on Places see it, with the eye a height above the ground and what is seen a height above it, as far as a distance, with the curve of the Earth. From where a wind turbine can be seen, what a lookout tower shows.

params.label: Eye above the ground
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: How high the eye is at each place, in metres: a number, or an attribute such as the height of a mast

params.label: Seen above the ground
params.hint: How high what is to be seen is, such as 0 for the ground or 150 for the top of a wind turbine

params.label: As far as
params.hint: How far the eye reaches, in metres

params.label: Each cell
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: How many of the places see each cell
1 where any of them sees, 0 elsewhere

params.label: The curve of the Earth
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Counted, with the bending of light

params.hint: Matters over kilometres: 5 km away the ground is 1.7 m lower

node_types.title: Interpolate points to raster
node_types.description: Makes a raster of values between points: heights from measured points, depths from soundings, noise or temperature from where it was measured. Linear in triangles (TIN), smooth by natural neighbours, by inverse distance, or the nearest point, at a cell size or on the cells of a raster on Like.

params.label: Value
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: Empty takes the height of the points. Or an attribute or expression, such as depth or the noise measured

params.label: Between the points
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Linear in triangles between the points (TIN)
Natural neighbours: smooth, through the points
Inverse distance: the nearest points, weighted

params.label: Cell size
params.hint: In the units of the coordinate system, such as metres. A raster connected to Like gives its cells instead

params.label: Nearest points
params.hint: For inverse distance: how many of the nearest points each cell takes

params.label: Power
params.hint: For inverse distance: higher lets the nearest points count for more

params.label: As far as
params.hint: Cells farther than this from every point are left empty. Empty: no limit. The triangles reach only between the points

node_types.title: Resample raster
node_types.description: Gives a raster other cells: a cell size, or the cells of a raster on Like, so that two rasters line up cell by cell for Raster calculator. The cell under the middle for classes, between the nearest for heights, or the mean or most common value to make it coarser.

params.label: Cell size
params.hint: The new size of the cells. A raster connected to Like gives its cells instead, so that the two line up cell by cell

params.label: The new value
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The cell under the middle: for classes
Between the four nearest cells: for heights and measures
The mean of the cells within: to make it coarser
The most common value within: classes made coarser

node_types.title: Fill empty cells
node_types.description: Fills the empty cells of a raster: holes in a terrain model under water or buildings, gaps between scans. From the cells around, weighted by how near they are, or with one value.

params.label: Fill
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: From the cells around, weighted by how near

params.label: As far as
params.hint: How many cells away the values are taken from. Holes wider than twice this stay empty in the middle

params.label: Value
params.hint: For one value: what every empty cell gets

node_types.title: Catchments and streams
node_types.description: Follows the water over a terrain model: the catchment above each outlet on Outlets, or the areas that drain off the terrain, as polygons with their area; the streams, with their order (Strahler) and the land they drain; and the flow, the area upstream of each cell, as a raster. Hollows are filled first, so that all water runs off.

params.label: Move outlets
params.hint: An outlet is moved to the cell with the most water running through it within this distance, so that it lies on the stream

params.label: Streams from
params.hint: Square kilometres: a cell with water from this much land or more is part of a stream

params.label: Without outlets, smallest
params.hint: Square kilometres: without outlets on Outlets, each area that drains to the edge of the terrain this large or larger is a catchment

node_types.title: Read satellite bands
node_types.description: Reads the bands of the satellite pictures that STAC search found, such as Sentinel-2 or Landsat, onto one grid over the area on Extent: a picture for each time, with the names of its bands, in the coordinate system and cell size you choose. Only the part of each file that covers the area is fetched over the web. The values are scaled to reflectance; bands of classes, such as scl, are kept as they are.

params.label: Bands
params.hint: The files of the items to read, by name, separated by commas: red, green, blue, nir, swir16 and scl at Element 84; B04, B08 and SCL at Copernicus

params.label: Cell size
params.hint: In metres. Sentinel-2 has 10 m for red, green, blue and nir, 20 m for the others

params.label: Coordinate system
params.hint: Of the grid. Empty: that of Extent, or SWEREF 99 TM when it is in degrees

params.label: Area in degrees
params.hint: West, south, east and north, when nothing is connected to Extent

params.label: Scale
params.hint: The values of the bands are multiplied by it, to reflectance from 0 to 1. Classes, such as scl, are not

params.label: Offset
params.hint: Added after the scale. Sentinel-2 from 2022 at Copernicus has −0.1; Element 84 has already taken it away

params.label: At most pictures
params.hint: Spread over the time, the least cloudy in each part; each is read over the web

node_types.title: Mask clouds
node_types.description: Empties the cells of clouds, their shadows, cirrus, and if asked snow and water, in every band of satellite pictures: by the scene classes (scl) of Sentinel-2 or the bits of QA_PIXEL of Landsat. The mask can be grown at the edges of clouds, and pictures with too little left are left out. Each picture gets the share that is clear.

params.label: Mask
params.shape: some of the values in choices: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Cells of these become empty in every band

params.label: Grow the mask by
params.hint: Cells around each masked cell, for the edges of clouds

params.label: Least clear share
params.hint: In percent: pictures with less of the area left are left out

node_types.title: Spectral index
node_types.description: Works out an index of the bands of each picture, such as NDVI for vegetation, NDWI for water, NDMI for moisture, NDBI for built-up land or NBR for burnt land, or an expression of your own with the names of the bands. The bands are found by their names in Sentinel-2 and Landsat alike. The index becomes the first band, and the others are kept or left out.

params.label: Index
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: EVI: vegetation where it is dense
SAVI: vegetation where the soil shows

params.hint: The bands are found by their names, for Sentinel-2 and Landsat alike

params.label: Expression
params.hint: With the names of the bands, such as (nir - red) / (nir + red)

params.label: Name of the band
params.hint: Empty: the name of the index

params.label: The other bands
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Composite over time
node_types.description: Puts satellite pictures of many times together into one, cell by cell: the median, which leaves out clouds that slipped through, the mean, the highest, the lowest, or all bands from the greenest time. For all the time at once, or a picture for each month, season or year. Count tells how many clear values each cell had.

params.label: Each cell gets
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Median: clouds and shadows that slipped through fall away
Greenest: all bands from the time with the highest NDVI

params.hint: Of the values it has over the time

params.label: Period
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: A picture for each, named by its first day

node_types.title: Check topology
node_types.description: Finds where areas that should lie edge to edge, such as properties or zones, overlap one another, and the gaps between them. Each overlap comes out with the two areas it lies in, and each gap as an area; the areas get how many others they overlap. With a boundary on Boundary, such as the municipality the areas should fill, gaps that open to the outside are found too, and what reaches beyond it comes out on Beyond. Overlaps and gaps smaller than a size are left out as noise, and holes larger than a size are taken to be meant.

params.label: Name the areas by
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: An attribute such as a property id. Empty: their numbers from 1

params.label: Leave out smaller than
params.hint: Overlaps and gaps of less area than this are not reported: the noise of coordinates

params.label: Gaps up to
params.hint: Holes larger than this are taken to be meant, such as a lake. Empty: every hole is a gap

node_types.title: Eliminate slivers
node_types.description: Merges small or thin areas, as overlays leave behind, into a neighbour: the one they share the longest border with, or the largest. The neighbour keeps its attributes. A sliver is smaller than an area, thinner than a roundness, or either. Slivers without a neighbour go to Left.

params.label: Smaller than
params.hint: Areas of less than this are slivers, in square units of the coordinate system

params.label: Or thinner than
params.hint: From 0 to 1: how round an area is, 1 for a circle. A long thin strip is below 0.1

params.label: Merged into
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The neighbour it shares the longest border with

params.hint: It keeps the attributes of that one

node_types.title: Merge lines
node_types.description: Merges lines that meet end to end into one line, where exactly two of them meet: the pieces of a street between crossings, or a river cut into many. Only lines with the same values of the attributes chosen are merged, and only those attributes are kept, with how many lines each is made of.

params.label: Group by
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Only lines with the same values are merged, such as the name of a street. Empty merges all

params.label: Ends within
params.hint: Ends this close count as the same point. 0: only ends that are equal

node_types.title: Points along lines
node_types.description: Puts points along each line at a distance from one another, from its start, and at its end if asked: stations along a road, or where to take a profile. Each point has the attributes of its line, the distance along it and the direction of the line there, clockwise from north.

params.label: Every
params.hint: A point at this distance along each line, from its start

params.label: First at
params.hint: The distance from the start of the first point

params.label: A point at the end
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Also where the line ends

node_types.title: Offset lines
node_types.description: Moves lines to the side by a distance, left of their direction or right with a negative number, keeping their shape: the edges of a road from its centre line, or two directions of traffic side by side. The distance can be an attribute or an expression.

params.label: Distance
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: To the left of the direction of the line; a negative number to the right. Or an attribute, such as half the width of a road

node_types.title: Locate along lines
node_types.description: Linear referencing: finds for each point the nearest line within a distance, and gives it the key of that line, how far along it the point is from its start (in metres, or as a share from 0 to 1) and how far to the side, + to the left. Such as where accidents lie along roads.

params.label: Line key
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Such as the id of a road, which each point gets. Empty: the number of the line

params.label: Within
params.hint: Points further from every line are left out

params.label: Measure as
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: A share from 0 at the start to 1 at the end

node_types.title: Place along lines
node_types.description: Linear referencing: places events that say where they are along a line, such as a speed limit from metre 120 to 860 of a road, as points or as the stretches of the line between from and to. The lines are found by a key, and the measures are metres or shares from 0 to 1, as in NVDB. They can be moved to the side.

params.label: Line key of the events
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Which line each event is on, such as a road id

params.label: Line key of the lines
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The same, among the attributes of the lines

params.label: From
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Where the event is along the line, or where a stretch begins

params.label: To
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Where a stretch ends. Empty: the events are points

params.label: Measures are
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: A share from 0 at the start to 1 at the end

params.label: To the side
params.hint: Moves points and stretches to the left of the line, or the right with a negative number

node_types.title: Pivot
node_types.description: Turns a long table wide: a row for each group, and a column for each value of an attribute, such as a column for each year with the population in it. When a group has several values for a column, the first, the sum, the mean, the lowest, the highest or how many.

params.label: A row for each
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Such as the municipality code

params.label: Columns from
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Each value becomes a column, such as each year

params.label: Values from
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: What goes in the columns, such as the population

params.label: When there are several
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Before the names
params.hint: Such as y_, so that a year becomes y_2026

node_types.title: Unpivot
node_types.description: Turns a wide table long: the attributes chosen become rows, each with the name of the attribute and its value, and the other attributes on every row. Such as a column for each year made into a row for each year, for a chart or a database.

params.label: Attributes to rows
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Each becomes a row of its own, such as one for each year

params.label: Name of the name column
params.hint: Gets the name of the attribute

params.label: Name of the value column
params.hint: Gets its value

params.label: Take away from the names
params.hint: Such as y_, so that y_2026 becomes 2026

params.label: Empty values
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Parse coordinates
node_types.description: Makes points of coordinates written as text, as people and programs write them: degrees, minutes and seconds (57°42'31"N 11°58'25"E), degrees and minutes (N 57° 42.520' E 11° 58.418'), decimal degrees with a point or a comma, or metres such as SWEREF 99 TM. The letters N, S, E and W, and Ö and V, say which is which; a third number is a height. What cannot be read goes to Failed with the reason.

params.label: Coordinates in
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port

params.label: Order
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Auto: by the letters, or as written below

params.hint: Without letters such as N and E: in degrees, latitude first unless a value is over 90; in metres, the larger is north

params.label: Coordinate system
params.hint: Of the coordinates: EPSG:4326 for degrees, EPSG:3006 for SWEREF 99 TM

node_types.title: Profile along line
node_types.description: The height of a surface, such as a terrain model, along each line: a point every few metres with its distance along the line and its height, for a chart of the profile, and the line itself in 3D with its length over the ground, lowest and highest point, and how much it climbs and descends. A path, a road or a planned pipe.

params.label: Every

params.label: Value
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

node_types.title: Volume between surfaces
node_types.description: How much lies above and below: the volume between a surface and a reference surface, such as the ground before and after, or a level, such as the bottom of a pit. Cut and fill in cubic metres, for each area connected to Areas or for the whole surface, and the difference cell by cell as a raster.

params.hint: The height to measure from when nothing is connected to Reference, such as the bottom of a pit or the level of a lake

node_types.title: Change height system
node_types.description: Changes heights from one height system to another with the grid of the geoid: from heights above the ellipsoid, as GNSS and many point clouds give them, to heights above sea level in RH 2000, or back, or between others such as NN2000 and EGM2008. The heights of the coordinates, of a point cloud, of a grid of heights and of a 3D model. The places stay as they are; Reproject moves them.

node_types.title: Outline from above
node_types.description: Makes 3D objects, such as walls, doors and furniture read from IFC, into areas in 2D: the shadow each object casts when lit from straight above, as one area with all that sticks out, such as the handle of a door. Seen from a height, such as 1 m above the floor of the storey, what is above it is left out, so that the wall over a door leaves a gap, as in a plan. Or only what the cut at that height goes through.

params.label: Height from

The lowest point of the object
The heights of the coordinate system

Only what the cut goes through, as in a plan drawing

node_types.title: Check against IDS
node_types.description: Checks the objects of an IFC model against an Information Delivery Specification (IDS 1.0): for each specification, the objects it applies to by class, attribute, property, material or storey, and what they must have, may have or must not have, with values as they are or as a list, a pattern or a range. Objects that meet every specification that applies go to Passed, the others to Failed with what they lack in ids_failed. The log tells how many meet each specification. Classifications are not read from IFC, so they cannot be checked, and the log says so.

params.label: IDS file

params.hint: The requirements as buildingSMART's Information Delivery Specification (.ids), such as a client's demands on the model

node_types.title: Real place for a game engine
node_types.description: Makes a real place ready for Unreal Engine, Unity or Godot. The terrain model on Heights becomes a square heightmap of 16 bits, as PNG and RAW, in a size the engine takes. The areas on Areas become masks for painting the ground, one for each kind, such as forest, water and fields. Trees, poles and buildings on Instances become a list of positions, each turned and sized, to place as instances. The roads on Roads become splines on the ground, and a mask of their width. Each in the units and axes of the engine, from a corner of the heightmap, with IMPORT.txt, which tells the scale and place to set when importing.

params.label: Engine

params.hint: The units, axes and sizes follow the engine

params.label: Folder

params.label: Size of the heightmap
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: As fine as the terrain model, up to the largest

params.hint: The nearest size the engine takes. The heightmap is square, over the whole terrain model; outside it, the lowest height

params.label: Masks by
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute of the areas that names their kind, such as forest, water or field: a mask for each kind. Empty: one mask of all the areas

params.label: Instances by
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: The attribute that names what stands there, such as tree, pole or house. Empty: instance

params.label: Height of instances
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Such as the height of a building or a tree, in metres, for its scale. Empty: none

params.label: Width of roads

params.hint: In metres: a number, or an attribute such as the width in NVDB. For the road mask and the splines

params.label: Name of roads
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: An attribute for the name of each spline. Empty: road and its number

node_types.title: Make Gaussian splats
node_types.description: Makes a point cloud, such as from a laser scanner or photos from a drone, a scene of Gaussian splats: each point the middle of a small, soft ellipse in its colour, as large as the spacing to its neighbours and, when flat, lying along the surface they make, so that walls, roofs and ground look whole. Write it as PLY or SPZ for viewers of splats, or see it in 3D with map data.

params.label: Neighbours
params.hint: How many of the nearest points give each splat its size and shape

params.label: Size
params.hint: Larger than 1 to close gaps between the points, smaller for sharper

params.label: Opacity
params.hint: From 0, clear, to 1, solid

params.label: Shape
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Flat along the surface, as a coin

params.hint: Flat splats follow walls and ground, and look like a surface

node_types.title: Fetch a place
node_types.description: Fetches heights and a picture from above of any place on Earth, by its name or its latitude and longitude: a square of the size given around it, in the UTM zone it lies in. The heights come from the Copernicus DEM GLO-30, 30 m, and the picture is made of the least cloudy Sentinel-2 pictures of a time, 10 m, the clouds taken away and the rest put together. Both are read over the web, only the part that is needed. Connect them to Shade terrain, Terrain model or Render 3D scene, and write a model for Blender.

params.label: Place
params.hint: A name, such as Kīlauea, Matterhorn or Isla Isabela, found with Nominatim of OpenStreetMap; or latitude and longitude, such as 19.41, -155.28

params.label: Size
params.hint: The side of the square around the place, in kilometres

params.label: Fetch
params.shape: some of the values in choices: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Heights from the Copernicus DEM, 30 m; a picture from Sentinel-2, 10 m

params.label: Time of the picture
params.hint: From and to, such as 2025-06-01/2025-09-30, when the place is green or free of snow. Empty: the year before today

params.label: Most clouds
params.hint: In percent: pictures with more are not used

params.label: At most pictures
params.hint: The least cloudy, put together where they are clear

params.label: Brightness
params.hint: More than 1 for a lighter picture, such as for dark lava or forest

params.label: Finder of places

params.label: Heights from
params.hint: The Copernicus DEM GLO-30 as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF, a file for each degree

params.label: Pictures from
params.hint: A STAC API with sentinel-2-l2a, its bands red, green, blue and scl

node_types.title: Hot spots
node_types.description: Finds where high values lie together, and low values: hot and cold spots, by the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic of each feature with its neighbours. Each feature gets gi_z (how far above or below what chance would give), gi_p, hot_spot, such as Hot spot, 99 %, and hot_class from -3 to 3, to colour from blue to red. Accidents counted in squares, illness in areas, prices of sold houses. The features should be in metres.

params.label: Value
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Such as the number of accidents in each square, or the rate of illness in each area

params.label: Neighbours
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The nearest, so many of them

params.hint: Which features count as near each other: those within a distance, or each feature's nearest few

params.label: Within
params.hint: In metres, between the middles of the features. Empty: as far as needed for every feature to have a neighbour

node_types.title: Spatial autocorrelation
node_types.description: Whether like values lie together, by Moran's I: on Summary the I of all the features, what chance would give, and a p-value from shuffling the values among the places; on Features each feature's local I, its p and its cluster: High-High and Low-Low where like lie together, High-Low and Low-High for one that stands out from its neighbours.

params.label: Value
params.shape: the name of one attribute of the stream on the port
params.hint: Such as the income or the share of elderly in each area

params.label: Neighbours
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The nearest, so many of them

params.hint: Which features count as near each other: those within a distance, or each feature's nearest few

params.label: Within
params.hint: In metres, between the middles of the features. Empty: as far as needed for every feature to have a neighbour

params.label: Permutations
params.hint: How many times the values are shuffled among the places to tell chance from pattern. More is surer and slower

params.label: Significant below
params.hint: The p-value under which a local cluster counts

node_types.title: Point clusters
node_types.description: Finds clusters of points by DBSCAN: points that have enough others within a distance, and those they reach, form a cluster, of any shape; points far from the rest belong to none. Each point gets its cluster and how many points it has, and the outline of each cluster comes on Clusters. Where the accidents gather, the trees of a forest stand, the visitors of a park stop.

params.label: Within
params.hint: In metres: points this close to each other belong together

params.label: At least
params.hint: Points within the distance of a point, itself counted, for it to be the core of a cluster. Points in no cluster get none

node_types.title: Reallocate between areas
node_types.description: Moves values from one division of the land to another that does not follow it, by how much of each area lies in the other: people from the squares of a population grid to the districts, jobs from DeSO to the catchments of the schools. Counts are shared out and added up, averages weighed by area. Points on From, such as addresses with their people, go whole to the area they lie in. Each area of To gets covered, the share of it that From covers.

params.label: Counts
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Such as people or jobs: shared out by how much of each area of From lies in each area of To, and added up

params.label: Averages
params.shape: names of attributes of the stream on the port: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: Such as a rate or a mean income: the mean in each area of To, weighed by how much of it each area of From covers

node_types.title: Tracks and stops
node_types.description: Makes points with a time into tracks, as from a GPS (GPX) or the AIS of ships: a line for each mover, broken where a pause is long, with its start, end, length and speed; each point with how far and how fast it came from the one before; and the stops, where the mover stayed within a radius for some minutes. Points that jump faster than the mover can go can be left out.

params.label: Time

params.hint: When each point was taken: ISO 8601 such as 2026-06-01T10:15:00Z, or seconds since 1970

params.label: Of whom

params.hint: What tells the movers apart, such as mmsi for ships or the name of a device. Empty: one mover

params.label: A new track after a pause of
params.hint: Minutes without a point. The track is broken there, so that no line is drawn across what is not known

params.label: A stop is within

params.label: For at least

params.label: Faster than this is a fault
params.hint: Km/h. A point the mover could not have reached so fast is left out, as GPS points that jump. Empty keeps all

node_types.title: Choose locations
node_types.description: Chooses the best places for one or more facilities among candidates, along the network: those that give the least travel in all for those on Demand, weighed such as by the people in each square, or that reach the most within some minutes. Facilities that are there already can be kept. Each chosen place gets its rank, how many it serves and their mean travel, and each on Demand its facility and travel. Where to put a new health centre, fire station or store.

params.label: How many to choose
params.hint: Places among Candidates, counting those that must be chosen

params.label: Best is
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: The least travel in all: the sum of each one's way to the nearest, weighed
The most reached within a limit

params.hint: Such as the number of people in a square of a population grid. Empty: each counts as one

params.label: Must be chosen when

params.hint: An attribute that is true, yes or 1 for the facilities that are there already. Empty: none

params.label: Direction

choices.label: Travelling to the facilities, as customers do
Travelling from the facilities, as an ambulance does

choices.label: Quickest: the time, by the speed

params.hint: Along the line as it is drawn, for the quickest route: an attribute such as F_Hogst_225 in NVDB, or a number

params.label: Speed against the line

params.hint: Such as B_ForbjudenFardriktning is null. Empty: always

node_types.title: Sum line lengths in areas
node_types.description: The length of the lines that lie in each area, as the length of the road network in each municipality: in all, or for each kind of line, such as each kind of road, as attributes on the areas or as a feature for each area and kind. A line that crosses a border counts in each area by the part of it inside. In metres or other units, on the ellipsoid when the coordinates are in degrees.

params.hint: Attributes of the lines, such as the kind of road. Empty sums all lines together

params.label: Unit

A feature for each area and kind

node_types.title: Classify image
node_types.description: Gives each cell of a picture with several bands, such as from Sentinel-2, a class: by itself, putting the cells in groups of like colours by k-means, numbered from the darkest, for you to name; or from examples, areas you drew of forest, water, field and town, each cell getting the class it is most like. On Classes, each class with its cells, area and mean of each band. Raster to areas then gives the areas of each class.

params.label: How
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: By itself: the cells are put in groups of like colours (k-means)
From examples: areas on Examples with their class, and each cell to the class it is most like

params.hint: Such as forest, water, field and town, or numbers

params.label: Bands

node_types.title: Hollows
node_types.description: Finds the hollows of a terrain model where water gathers and stays in a cloudburst, as it would if it could not soak away: each with its greatest depth, the water it holds when full, its area, its bottom and the height at which it runs over. On Depth, how deep the water stands in each cell when every hollow is full. Join buildings to Hollows to see which lie where water gathers; Catchments and streams shows the way it runs there.

params.label: At least as deep as

node_types.title: Tool

node_types.description: For maps: illuminated contours, after Kitiro Tanaka: the contour lines of the heights on Heights, light where the slope faces the light and dark where it faces away, widest where they face it squarely, over bands of colour between the heights. The terrain stands out as in relief. The picture has coordinates; the pieces of line come out on Lines with their height and light.

params.label: Height between lines

params.label: Lines through the height
params.hint: One line goes through this height, the others every interval from it

params.label: Light from

params.label: Line width
params.hint: The widest line, in pixels, where a slope faces the light or turns from it squarely

params.label: Smoothing
params.hint: How many times the heights are evened out over their neighbours first, for calm lines over flat land. 0 keeps every bump

params.label: Bands
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Land: green to brown to light

params.label: Light

node_types.title: Merge rasters
node_types.description: Puts the rasters connected to Rasters together into one: pictures, such as tiles of an orthophoto, or grids, such as tiles of a terrain model. Where they overlap, the one connected first is on top. Rasters in another coordinate system are reprojected to that of the first.

node_types.title: Generalize raster
node_types.description: Makes a raster coarser: a number of cells across and down become one, with their mean, the most common value for classes such as land cover, the median, the smallest, the largest or the sum. Pictures get the mean colour.

params.label: Cells into one
params.hint: How many cells across and down become one: 4 makes 1 m cells into 4 m cells, sixteen into one

params.label: The new value
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Majority: the most common value, for classes

params.hint: Empty cells are left out. A new cell is empty only when all its cells are

node_types.title: Raster calculator
node_types.description: Counts cell by cell with the rasters connected to Rasters, A the first and B the second: A + B, A - B, A * B, A / B, and anything an expression can do, such as if(A > 100, B, null), max(A, B) or sqrt(A). The result has the cells of A, where the rasters overlap.

params.label: Expression
params.hint: A is the raster connected first, B the second, and so on. Such as (A - B) / A * 100, if(A > 100, B, null) or max(A, B, C). Band 2 of A is A_2

params.label: The result covers
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Its cells are those of A. The other rasters are reprojected and read at the middle of each

params.label: An empty cell
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Where a raster has no value. coalesce(B, 0) does the same for one of them

node_types.title: Contour lines

params.label: Start at

params.label: Make
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

params.label: Height attribute
params.hint: The height of each line. Areas get it with _min and _max after it

node_types.title: Shortest route
node_types.description: Finds the shortest or quickest route along a network of lines, such as the roads of NVDB, from each feature on From to the nearest feature on To, or to every one, with Dijkstra's algorithm. The lines are joined where their ends meet. Points are put on the nearest place of the nearest line. One-way roads and speeds come from attributes of the network. The routes are lines with the attributes of both ends, the length and the time; those with no route go to Unreached.

params.label: Routes
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Every one gives a route for each pair, as many as From times To

params.label: Rules of the road
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Ready rules for OpenStreetMap or NVDB: one-way streets, roundabouts, speed limits and which roads may be used, by how one travels. My own: the conditions and speeds below

params.label: Travelling
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: With ready rules: by car at the speed limits, by bicycle at 18 km/h, on foot at 5 km/h

params.label: Keep away from
params.shape: some of the values in choices: a list of strings, or one string separated by commas
params.hint: With ready rules, these roads are left out of the network

params.label: By
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Quickest: the time, by the speed

params.label: Speed in km/h
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: Along the line as it is drawn, for the quickest route: an attribute such as F_Hogst_225 in NVDB, or a number

params.label: Speed against the line
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: Against the way the line is drawn, such as B_Hogst_225 in NVDB. Empty uses the speed along it

params.label: Speed where none is given
params.hint: In km/h, where the speed is empty or 0

params.label: May be travelled along the line when
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: A condition for one-way roads, such as F_ForbjudenFardriktning is null. Empty: always

params.label: May be travelled against the line when
params.shape: an expression over the attributes of the stream on the port; text in 'single quotes', names with spaces in "double quotes"
params.hint: Such as B_ForbjudenFardriktning is null. Empty: always

params.label: Farthest from the network, in metres
params.hint: A point is put on the nearest place of the nearest line. One farther away than this is not reached

params.label: Line ends that meet, within
params.hint: In metres. Lines are joined where their ends are this close, not where they only cross, as at a bridge

node_types.title: Run model
node_types.description: Runs another model, so that work can be split into models of their own and run as a chain: fetch, then prepare, then publish. It waits until the other model has run, and what is connected after it runs after that; or it starts the other model by itself and goes on. Connect a stream to After to run it after that stream is done. The log of the other model comes in this log, and Result tells how each of its nodes went.

params.label: Model
params.shape: a file, a folder, a pattern with * or a web address; relative paths start at the folder of the model
params.hint: The model to run, an .ographis file (or .json, as before 0.75). Paths in it start from its own folder

params.label: This model
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string

choices.label: Wait until it has run, then go on
Start it and go on at once

params.hint: Started without waiting, it runs by itself with og, and writes its log beside it

params.label: Variables
params.hint: Values for variables of the other model: year=2026; county=14. $(name) gives a variable of this model

params.label: If it fails
params.shape: one of the values in choices, as a string
params.hint: Whether what comes after Run model runs when a node of the other model fails
